verdict: Hims & Hers grew revenue 28% to $618M and stayed profitable — $21M of net income with 2.5 million subscribers — closing a year in which revenue jumped 59% to $2.35B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $618M, vs $481M a year ago

kpis.label: Subscribers
kpis.note: Up 13% YoY — people on a recurring subscription plan at year end

segments.name: Online revenue
segments.note: Sales through the website and apps — telehealth subscriptions for weight loss, hair, skin, sexual health and other treatments, plus the products that go with them.

segments.name: Wholesale revenue
segments.note: Sales of products through retail stores and platform partners — a small, shrinking side channel.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Ads and the cost of signing up new customers — the biggest running cost, at 39% of sales.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Fulfilling orders, running pharmacies and supporting customers.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building the app, website and clinical tools, and paying the engineers behind them.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin; includes $20M of stock pay.

takeaways.title: A breakout year
takeaways.text: Q4 revenue rose 28% to $618M, capping a year in which revenue jumped 59% to $2.35B and Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $318M. Monthly revenue per subscriber rose 11% to $83.

takeaways.title: Margins are thinner
takeaways.text: Gross margin was 72%, down from 77% a year ago, as the product mix shifted — profitability now depends on marketing staying efficient at 39% of sales.

takeaways.title: Cash went into buildings
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was +$66M, but free cash flow was −$3M in Q4: the company spent $59M in the quarter on property and equipment, building its own fulfillment and pharmacy capacity.

otherDetail: Other income was $9.2M, net: equity securities the company holds gained $4.4M in value and other income added $6.4M, partly offset by a $1.6M rise in the value of liabilities it owes.
footerNote: Filed in thousands; shown in $M to three decimals so the lines add up.
